---
title: "Figure 4—figure supplement 8 — residual autocorrelation over the design space: the gating memory LSE and NR leave in the data"
author: "Luciano Moffatt"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document
---

<!--
THE GATING-MEMORY MAP. The integral autocorrelation lag of the standardised residual r_std =
(patch - y_mean)/sqrt(y_var), one scalar per cell, mapped over the same (Delta*k_off, noise) plane as
Figure 4, N_ch on columns, algorithm on rows. This is Luciano's gating-noise indicator, and unlike
the per-cell ACF (Figure 3-supplement 3) it is a scalar the battery ALREADY emits per cell
(Report_integral_r_std, statistic = integral_correlation_lag), so it sweeps the whole grid.

WHAT IT IS. integral_correlation_lag = C(0)^{-1/2} Omega C(0)^{-1/2} with C(0) the residual variance
and Omega the kernel summed over all lags — the Sokal/Kish integrated autocorrelation time, in
normalized form. It is 1 for a white residual and grows with temporal memory: value ~ 1 + 2*sum_k
rho_resid(k).

WHY IT READS GATING. The recorded current is temporally-correlated gating plus white instrumental
noise, so rho_resid(k) = rho_gating(k) * V_gate/(V_gate + V_inst). The integral lag is therefore large
where gating dominates and falls to 1 as instrumental noise whitens the residual — a direct read of
how much gating signal is present, from the data against the fitted mean, needing no likelihood.

WHAT THE ROWS SAY (measured). IR is 1 to three digits everywhere (its recursion has absorbed the
gating correlation: nothing left in the residual). R is just above 1. LSE and NR retain the memory,
6-9 at low noise, and FALL toward 1 as noise rises (LSE 9.3 -> 2.7, NR 5.9 -> 1.6 across noise 0.1 to
100): the whitening Luciano predicted. LSE carries MORE memory than NR at low noise because it divides
the residual by a single global variance while NR at least rescales per time. The gap between the
naive pair (LSE, NR) and the recursive pair (R, IR) is the recursion's whole job, seen in the data.

All plane/scale/facet machinery is shared from figure_4_common.R.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

```{r common, include=FALSE}
source("figure_4_common.R")
```

```{r scale}
# Sequential, 1 = white residual, growing with memory. bandcols would centre white on the band
# containing 0 in log space (value 1), which is exactly right here since a white residual IS the
# neutral case — but the data barely dips below 1 (IR min 0.994), so build it one-sided like the SE
# supplement to keep dark = more memory. Range measured 0.99 to 9.45.
LAG_LIN    <- c(1, 1.15, 1.3, 1.5, 2, 3, 5, 8, 12)
LAG_BREAKS <- log10(LAG_LIN)
LAG_PAL    <- colorRampPalette(RAMP[7:13], space = "Lab")(length(LAG_LIN) - 1)
LAG_LAB    <- fmt_big(LAG_LIN)
LAG_SOL    <- 1.5    # noticeable memory
LAG_DSH    <- 3      # strong memory
```

```{r data}
lag_resid <- imap_dfr(GRID_BY_ALGO, function(g, a) if (!nrow(g)) tibble() else
  pmap_dfr(g, function(nch, z) {
    d <- read.csv(findf(nch, a, z, "battery_sim_G"), skip = 1) %>%
      filter(component_path == "Probit_statistics_Report_integral_r_std",
             statistic == "integral_correlation_lag", probit == "mean")
    tibble(algo = a, noise = z, Num_ch = nch, interval_in_tau = d$interval_in_tau, v = d$value)
  })) %>%
  group_by(algo, noise, Num_ch, interval_in_tau) %>% summarise(m = mean(v), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(param = "resid",            # single synthetic parameter: the residual is not per-parameter
         lx = log10(interval_in_tau), ly = log10(as.numeric(noise)),
         nchf = factor(paste0("N[ch]==", Num_ch), levels = paste0("N[ch]==", NCHS)))

PARAM_MATH["resid"] <- "r[std]"
cat("residual integral-lag by algorithm and noise (median over N_ch and interval):\n")
print(as.data.frame(lag_resid %>% group_by(algo, noise) %>% summarise(m = median(m), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = algo, values_from = m)), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)
sat(log10(lag_resid$m), min(LAG_BREAKS), max(LAG_BREAKS), "residual integral-lag")
```

```{r render, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5.2}
hC <- map_height(1, 0.475)
g <- btitle("Residual autocorrelation (integral lag of r_std)") /
     mapblock(lag_resid, function(d) log10(d$m), LAG_PAL, LAG_BREAKS, "resid",
              top = TRUE, bottom = TRUE, iso_sol = log10(LAG_SOL), iso_dsh = log10(LAG_DSH)) /
     colorbar(LAG_PAL, LAG_LAB, "integral lag", LAG_LIN, sol = LAG_SOL, dsh = LAG_DSH)
hs <- c(0.16, hC, 0.28)
g <- g + plot_layout(heights = hs)
g
ggsave("Figure_4_supplement_8.pdf", g, width = 7.0, height = sum(hs))
```
